chunks: And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
One who performs a deed for the sake of people, his reward is with the people.
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Almighty Allah said: One who performs a deed for Me and for others, he has done it for others.

key_terms.رِيَاءٍ: Showoff or performing deeds to be seen by others
key_terms.شِرْكٌ: Polytheism or associating partners with God

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between performing a deed for God versus for people in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-Amal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) distinction between *ikhlas* (sincerity) and *riya'* (showoff), noting that deeds done for public approval are nullified of divine reward and attributed to the observers. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly view that *riya'* constitutes a minor or major *shirk* depending on its depth, as the heart’s intention determines the ultimate beneficiary of the action. The cited Divine saying reinforces that mixed intentions result in the deed being claimed by the secondary motive, emphasizing the necessity of purifying the heart for Allah alone.
